verdict.rationale: Zero's README makes a first-party privacy statement that it does not track, collect, or sell user data. It also discloses that users' emails are stored in their Durable Object and an R2 bucket, which covers part of the transparency half of the story. Nothing in the evidence documents blocking sender tracking or read pixels, by default or otherwise, and that is the core protection the story asks for. Missing for 10: tracking-pixel or remote-image blocking, default-on sender-tracking protection, a detailed privacy policy or data-handling documentation, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a switcher, the client protects me from senders' tracking — blocking read pixels by default — and is transparent about what it does with my mail data

citations.quote: Zero does not track, collect, or sell your data in any way.
